original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-good-dga}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $(\mathcal{B}, \text{d})$ be a differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebra.
There exists a quasi-isomorphism of differential graded $\mathcal{O}$-algebras
$(\mathcal{A}, \text{d}) \to (\mathcal{B}, \text{d})$ such that
$\mathcal{A}$ is graded flat and K-flat as a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules
and such that the same is true after pullback by any morphism of
ringed topoi.

semantic_review_note: Every differential graded O-algebra B on a ringed site admits a quasi-isomorphic DG algebra A that is BOTH graded-flat and K-flat as O-complex, with these flatness properties still holding after pullback by ANY ringed-topos morphism. The strengthened universal pullback condition is retained.
